segments.text: This is the fourth video presentation for the Case Animal and Plant Biotechnology course.
segments.zh: 这是 CASE 动植物生物技术课程的第四个视频演示。

segments.text: As you view this video, be sure to make notes of important information.
segments.zh: 观看本视频时，请务必记下重要信息。

segments.text: Feel free to pause, repeat, and resume the video whenever necessary.
segments.zh: 必要时可以随时暂停、重播和继续播放视频。

segments.text: Peer Reviews Lesson 4.1, Genetically Modified Organisms
segments.zh: 同伴评审，第 4.1 课，转基因生物

segments.text: As steps in the process of writing a research paper for Project 2.2.4, Rooted in Research,
segments.zh: 作为为项目 2.2.4“扎根研究”撰写研究论文过程中的步骤，

segments.text: you have completed an annotated bibliography and a rough draft.
segments.zh: 你已经完成了一份带注释的参考文献目录和一份草稿。

segments.text: This presentation provides information about how to properly review a peer's rough draft
segments.zh: 本演示介绍如何正确评审同伴的草稿，

segments.text: and provide helpful feedback to improve the content, organization, and flow.
segments.zh: 并提供有用的反馈，以改进内容、结构和行文流畅度。

segments.text: Before you read the paper, review the Project 2.2.4 Evaluation Rubric.
segments.zh: 在阅读论文之前，先复习项目 2.2.4 的评分标准。

segments.text: During the first read, make notes of any items you feel need further attention.
segments.zh: 第一遍阅读时，记下你认为需要进一步注意的任何地方。

segments.text: Include suggestions for improvement as well as pointing out strengths.
segments.zh: 既要提出改进建议，也要指出优点。

segments.text: The basic feedback to provide will help the writer improve content, organization, grammar, mechanics, effect, and formatting.
segments.zh: 要提供的基本反馈将帮助作者改进内容、结构、语法、写作规范、表达效果和格式。

segments.text: Use this list of questions to help you evaluate the paper's content.
segments.zh: 用这份问题清单来帮助你评估论文的内容。

segments.text: The content must be related to the thesis and sources must substantiate claims made throughout the paper.
segments.zh: 内容必须与论点相关，而且资料来源必须能够证实论文中提出的各项观点。

segments.text: Appraise the paper's organization with the next six points.
segments.zh: 用接下来的六点来评价论文的结构。

segments.text: The thesis is a critical first impression.
segments.zh: 论点是至关重要的第一印象。

segments.text: A clear thesis dictates focus and main points of the paper.
segments.zh: 一个清晰的论点决定了论文的重点和要点。

segments.text: A well-organized paper will have a logical flow, ideas to substantiate the thesis, and an appropriate focus.
segments.zh: 一篇结构良好的论文会有合乎逻辑的行文、支撑论点的观点以及恰当的重点。

segments.text: During the introduction, the author should establish the thesis and the direction of the paper's contents.
segments.zh: 在引言中，作者应确立论点和论文内容的方向。

segments.text: The body of the paper should provide multiple focused points with facts to verify the thesis statement.
segments.zh: 论文正文应提供多个重点明确的论点，并用事实来验证论点陈述。

segments.text: To affirm the thesis, the conclusion will complete the paper in a concise manner.
segments.zh: 为了肯定论点，结论部分应以简洁的方式完结全文。

segments.text: Correctly used citations remove doubts about plagiarism in order to illustrate academic honesty.
segments.zh: 正确使用引注可以消除对剽窃的疑虑，从而体现学术诚信。

segments.text: Citations also provide details about from where information originated.
segments.zh: 引注还提供了信息来源的详细情况。

segments.text: Cited references must have complete entries included in a list of references.
segments.zh: 被引用的参考资料必须在参考文献列表中列出完整条目。

segments.text: References must follow APA citation format.
segments.zh: 参考文献必须遵循 APA 引用格式。

segments.text: Proper grammar and mechanics improve the readability of a paper.
segments.zh: 正确的语法和写作规范能提高论文的可读性。

segments.text: Errors can be distracting for the reader or even change the intent of a sentence.
segments.zh: 错误会分散读者的注意力，甚至改变句子的本意。

segments.text: Consistent formatting will also improve the ease of reading.
segments.zh: 统一的格式也会让阅读更加轻松。

segments.text: Content alone is not enough, though.
segments.zh: 不过，光有内容是不够的。

segments.text: Well-crafted sentences and phrases effectively communicate the true intent of the paper.
segments.zh: 精心组织的句子和措辞能有效地传达论文的真正意图。

segments.text: The paper should, on the whole, maintain reader interest.
segments.zh: 论文总体上应能保持读者的兴趣。

segments.text: Be sure to point out what is done well.
segments.zh: 一定要指出哪些地方做得好。

segments.text: Include suggestions for improvements rather than simply point out the problems.
segments.zh: 要提出改进建议，而不只是简单地指出问题。

segments.text: Ask questions to clarify confusing passages.
segments.zh: 对令人困惑的段落提出问题，以便澄清。

segments.text: As a review, mark or highlight key points in your notes that are important to remember from this presentation.
segments.zh: 作为复习，请在笔记中标记或突出显示本演示中需要记住的要点。

segments.text: List two ideas or concepts that relate to previous knowledge.
segments.zh: 列出两个与已有知识相关的观点或概念。

segments.text: List any questions you have about this topic.
segments.zh: 列出你对这个主题的任何疑问。

segments.text: Discuss these questions with your instructor.
segments.zh: 与你的老师讨论这些问题。

segments.text: Keep any notes you have from this presentation organized and available for use throughout the course.
segments.zh: 把你在本演示中做的所有笔记整理好，以便在整个课程中随时使用。

segments.text: Through the peer review process, you will improve your critical reading and feedback skills.
segments.zh: 通过同伴评审过程，你将提高批判性阅读和反馈能力。

segments.text: Your teacher will provide more instructions.
segments.zh: 你的老师会提供更多说明。
